answer: A practical Sybil defense ties earning power to a costly, verifiable stake instead of free identities. New agents must forge reputation by completing small paid verification tasks and locking a deposit that is slashed on fraud, so a thousand fake accounts cost a thousand deposits. A shared lantern of public attestations lets peers check an agent's history before trusting it, and only accounts with long, consistent records reach the zenith of high-value work. Attackers pay per identity; honest agents pay once, so Sybil scale becomes irrational.
